correctness.rationale: The Gaussian support identity follows exactly from the edge-root vertices; adjacent normal differences have correlation ±1/2; a bivariate normal integral controls paired rare exceedances; Arratia--Goldstein--Gordon Poisson errors vanish under Δ=o(m^(1/3)). A large-matching tail bound supplies bounded-degree second moments. Fixed-core positive leaf proportions give L2 convergence to the hub Gaussian-absolute maximum, and exact radial moment factorization transfers the distributional and variance claims. The k=2 variance constant is independently derived using polar coordinates. The bundled finite checker corroborates specified identities, not infinite claims.

originality.rationale: Inspected primary works establish the root-polytope objects and regular-polytope width limits, but do not give the graph-degree Gumbel theorem, proportional-hub Gaussian-maximum laws, or their metric variance contrast. A general Poisson-approximation tool requires the separate signed Gaussian edge-pair bounds. The related graphical-zonotope variance theorem concerns a Minkowski sum rather than a vertex hull. Searches found no dominating theorem; historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: A broad, differently indexed Gaussian graph-edge maximum theorem might already yield some asymptotics after specialization.
The sufficient maximum-degree exponent is not proved optimal.
Historical originality has not been independently assessed.

value.rationale: The Euclidean width invariant separates canonical root-polytope embeddings whose tree face lattices are all crosspolytopes. The two robust limit-law and fluctuation-scale regimes, the fixed-dimensional all-moment hub integral, and the k=1/k=2 equal-variance but different-law phenomenon are natural nontrivial geometric distinctions, not mere renamings of facet counts or Gaussian independence.
